answer: Submissions that land within 260 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The knoll detector writes to reef, and forge shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, and therefore the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 16 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 18 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
